Put $c=f(1)$. Setting $y=1$ gives $f(cx)=f(x)$. If $c>1$, iterating this equality contradicts the limit; if $c<1$, use $f(x/c)=f(x)$ instead. Hence $c=1$.

Setting $x=1$ now gives $f(f(y))=y$. Substituting $f(y)$ for $y$ in the original equation gives $f(xy)=f(x)f(y)$. In particular $f(1/t)=1/f(t)$.

For any $x$, put $k=xf(x)$. The original equation gives $f(k)=k$. If $k>1$, multiplicativity gives $f(k^n)=k^n$, contradicting the limit. If $k<1$, the same contradiction applies to the fixed point $1/k>1$. Therefore $xf(x)=1$ for every $x$. The function $f(x)=1/x$ directly satisfies both conditions and is the unique answer.
